brief.headline: Aluminium made its fifth new cycle high in eight sessions and printed the highest official cash since 22-June - and the front-end premium that appeared on Monday was gone within a single session, with cash settling BELOW the three-month. The genuinely new fact today is upstream rather than on the exchange: the largest alumina refinery outside China cut output to half on a gas-supply failure, which puts the cheap alumina that has quietly driven smelter margins all year directly at risk.
bullets: WHAT MOVED. LME cash aluminium settled $3,373.00 on 11-August, up $45.50 (+1.37%), the highest official cash settlement since 22-June-2026 and a fifth new cycle high in eight sessions; the three-month settled $3,374.00, up $53.50 (+1.61%). Exchange stock fell another 1,500 t to 253,400 t - a 30th consecutive draw, and on the newswire framing the lowest since November 1990. Four of the five base metals rose together on the three-month official, with only nickel lower.

WHY THE CURVE MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE TODAY. Because the three-month rose MORE than cash, the front end flipped straight back out of Monday's $7.00 backwardation into a $1.00 contango - spread and flat price moved in OPPOSITE directions. Three of the eight August sessions have now closed in contango, and the front end has not held a premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August, across five new highs. A market willing to pay more for metal in three months than for metal today is being driven by expectation rather than prompt physical need. That expectation may prove right - but until the curve agrees, this remains a positioning-led move.

THE UPSTREAM SHOCK IS THE REAL NEWS. Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte in Para, Brazil - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - has cut production to 50 percent after its gas supplier notified disruptions to natural gas availability, guiding a potential Q3 hit of US$75-100m to its Bauxite & Alumina segment. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina capacity is running at half rate. Alumina has been the quiet engine of producer margins in 2026 precisely because it has been cheap - around 10-11% of the metal price against a 15-17% decade norm. This is the first credible threat to that, and it lands on top of a Chinese alumina cost floor already rising on bauxite.

WHAT TO WATCH NEXT. First, today's 13:20 ring: whether the curve stabilises or posts a fourth August contango while price keeps climbing - a widening contango into new highs would be the clearest evidence yet that the physical market is not following. Second, any public seaborne alumina print in the days after the Alunorte disclosure, which converts a supply headline into a cost fact. Third, the monthly carbon settlement window around the 17th-18th, with crude near $89 and coal up roughly 16% year-on-year feeding the anode complex.

kpis.label: Cash-3M spread
kpis.note: THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT NUMBER ON THIS PAGE TODAY, AND IT WENT THE WRONG WAY. Cash $3,373.00 is $1.00 BELOW 3-month $3,374.00, a $1.00 CONTANGO, against a $7.00 BACKWARDATION on 10-August. CONVENTION, STATED EXPLICITLY: cash above 3M is BACKWARDATION and signals prompt tightness; cash below 3M is CONTANGO and signals prompt comfort. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS TODAY - flat price made a fifth new cycle high while the front end gave up its entire premium - and this desk flagged exactly that outcome yesterday as the clean test, writing that the $7.00 was 'one session old' and that 'single-session structure flips reverse routinely'. IT REVERSED IN ONE SESSION. THE AUGUST SEQUENCE NOW READS: +$48.00, +$34.50, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$1.00, a $0.50 CONTANGO, +$7.00, and now a $1.00 CONTANGO. Three of the eight August sessions have closed in contango and the front end has not held a premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August. THE HONEST READ, AND IT IS NOT THE COMFORTABLE ONE: the roughly $35/t of front-end structure written off on 05-August has now failed to rebuild for six sessions out of seven, across FIVE new flat-price highs. A market that will pay progressively more for metal in three months but not for metal today is being driven by expectation rather than by prompt physical need. That is not a reason to dismiss the rally - the expectation may well be correct, and Alunorte plus a 30th consecutive stock draw are real - but it is the reason to keep calling this a positioning-led move until the curve says otherwise. PROPORTION, BOTH WAYS: $1.00 is 0.03% of cash and is effectively FLAT, not a stress signal; the correct word is 'no premium', not 'surplus'. avg = the July-2026 mean cash-3M spread of +$6.48 across the 23 published July sessions, so today sits $7.48 BELOW the July norm.

lme.commentary: THE 11-AUGUST OFFICIAL DELIVERED THE STRONGEST FLAT PRICE OF THE CYCLE AND THE WEAKEST STRUCTURE OF THE WEEK, AT THE SAME TIME. Cash settled $3,373.00 (+$45.50, +1.37%) and the three-month $3,374.00 (+$53.50, +1.61%), both the highest official prints since 22-June-2026. Because the three-month outran cash, the $7.00 backwardation established on 10-August collapsed into a $1.00 CONTANGO in a single session - exactly the reversal this page named yesterday as the clean test, and it failed the test. THE SEQUENCE IS NOW UNAMBIGUOUS AND SHOULD BE READ WITHOUT FLATTERY: since the 05-August routing announcement removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure, the front end has rebuilt for exactly one session out of seven, while flat price has posted FIVE new cycle highs. Structure is not confirming price. THE PHYSICAL SIDE IS STILL GENUINELY TIGHT AND THAT TENSION IS THE STORY: stock fell a 30th consecutive day, down 1,500 t to 253,400 t, a level SMM's 12-August wire frames as the lowest since November 1990. Six of the last seven sessions have drawn exactly 1,500 t - steady, not accelerating. So the inventory picture argues tight and the curve argues comfortable, and the reconciliation is almost certainly location and form: metal exists, but the marginal prompt buyer is not paying up for it. CROSS-COMPLEX, ALUMINIUM IS THE STRUCTURAL LAGGARD DESPITE LEADING ON PRICE. Copper's backwardation widened to $207.50 and zinc's to $81.00 while aluminium's disappeared. Copper drew a further 3,750 t to 214,550 t. In a complex that is tightening at the front, aluminium's front end went the other way. TECHNICALLY, THE THREE-MONTH LANDED WITHIN $1.00 OF THE WAVE-(v) EQUALITY OBJECTIVE OF $3,373 that this page has carried for a week; the next published objective is the 1.618x extension at $3,392. SOURCE INTEGRITY: the English overview was serving a stale 10-August board at this compile; the cache-busted German overview and the cache-busted per-metal tables both carried 11-August and agree exactly. That is the fourth logged cache incident and the second on an overview page.

drivers.text: The front end surrendered its premium again - the single most important premium-relevant fact today — The 11-August official put cash at $3,373.00 against a three-month of $3,374.00, a $1.00 CONTANGO, reversing the $7.00 backwardation of 10-August in one session. Regional premiums are prompt physical prices, so a front end that will not hold a premium for two consecutive sessions - it has not since 04-August - is the most direct available evidence against a higher Q4 settlement. Three of the eight August sessions have closed in contango, and across FIVE new flat-price highs the prompt premium has rebuilt exactly once.
drivers.source: Westmetall - LME official settlements, 11-Aug-2026 board (German overview, cache-busted)

drivers.text: The Hormuz talks are now publicly described as stalled, which cuts the other way — SMM's 12-August wire attributes aluminium's move to its highest since June explicitly to 'stalled US-Iran negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz', a route that once carried around 10% of global aluminium production, and pairs it with LME inventories near 250,000 t described as the lowest since November 1990. It also carries Norsk Hydro's public warning that the global deficit could exceed 900,000 t this year if Hormuz trade is not normalised. For a Q4 premium negotiation opening in late August, a corridor that is stalled rather than reopening is the sellers' strongest single argument.
drivers.source: SMM - Aluminum climbs above $3,300 as stalled Hormuz talks and record-low inventories fuel supply fears (12-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: A 6.3 Mt/y alumina refinery at half rate is new, dated and material — Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte cut production to 50 percent after gas supplier CELBA notified disruptions to natural gas availability, guiding a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. This does not move a metal premium directly - it is an alumina event - but it raises the delivered cost of the marginal tonne of metal for any smelter buying alumina on the seaborne market, and it removes one of the arguments buyers have used all year, namely that producers are already earning historically wide margins on cheap alumina.
drivers.source: Norsk Hydro - Alunorte reduces alumina production on natural gas supply disruptions (11-Aug-2026)

drivers.text: The Western supply pipeline met its first legal obstacle, and Asian capacity kept advancing — Oklahoma's Attorney General filed on 11-August for a preliminary injunction halting construction of the US$4bn, >750 kt/y Inola smelter, a 60:40 EGA-Century venture, ahead of the town's construction moratorium expiring 28-August; the developers dispute the claims. In the same 24 hours SMM reported Taijing Aluminum Indonesia's 600 kt Morowali project advancing, with the 300 kt first phase expected to commence production in 2026. The structural cap on any Q4 premium is still returning supply - but the composition is shifting East, and Western additions are no longer a safe assumption.
drivers.source: SMM - Oklahoma AG seeks injunction to halt $4B aluminum smelter project (12-Aug-2026)

prices.label: Alumina FOB East Australia (SMM reported trade)
prices.note: HELD AT $356/mt FOB EAST AUSTRALIA (SMM-reported transaction of 30,000 mt for September loading dealt 05-Aug-2026, published 06-Aug). THE DOMINANT ALUMINA FACT THIS RUN IS A SUPPLY EVENT, NOT A PRICE PRINT. Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte in Barcarena, Para - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - has REDUCED PRODUCTION TO 50 PERCENT after gas supplier CELBA (New Fortress Group), which also owns the Barcarena gas terminal infrastructure, notified disruptions to natural gas availability. Contingency measures are spot gas purchases and a request for direct access to the Barcarena LNG receiving and regasification terminal; Hydro will ramp back up 'as soon as gas availability normalizes' and guides a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million while calling the full impact uncertain. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina is therefore off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period. NO PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRICE PRINT DATED AFTER THE DISCLOSURE WAS FOUND AT THIS COMPILE, so NO VALUE ON THIS PANEL IS CHANGED - the event is recorded, the price is not invented. The next public transaction print is the datapoint that converts this headline into a cost fact. THE OTHER RECENT PRINT, STATED SEPARATELY BECAUSE THE BASIS DIFFERS AND MUST NOT BE BLENDED: SMM published on 11-August that 30,000 mt traded at $365/mt CIF MALAYSIA for September shipment, dealt 07-Aug-2026. CIF Malaysia is a delivered price including freight; FOB East Australia is a load-port price, so the $9/mt gap is broadly freight rather than a $9/mt rally. The honest read on the two together is that the seaborne market held around the mid-$350s FOB through the first week of August. MARGIN CONTEXT AT THE NEW METAL PRICE: against the 11-August LME three-month official of $3,374.00 the FOB mark sits at about 10.6% of the metal price and the CIF mark at about 10.8%, both still well below the decade rule of thumb of roughly 15-17%. On the marks available the alumina leg remains a TAILWIND to smelter economics - but Alunorte is the first credible threat to that tailwind this year, and the ratio is a lagging read on a supply event that is one day old.

prices.label: SMM Alumina Index (China)
prices.note: SMM Alumina Index (China domestic). Carried at its stated date - no fresher public print was returned this run. THE MOST USEFUL RECENT CHINESE ALUMINA DATAPOINT REMAINS A COST NUMBER, NOT A PRICE: SMM published on 11-August that China's national weighted-average FULL production cost for alumina was RMB 2,718/mt in July, UP RMB 37/mt month-on-month, with the weighted-average CASH cost at RMB 2,544/mt. SMM guides August full cost to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and cash cost to RMB 2,530-2,650/mt. The rise is attributed almost entirely to bauxite - higher imported CIF costs on elevated ocean freight plus the Guinea rainy season, and persistently tight domestic ore after mining-accident after-effects slowed restarts - partly offset by a small decline in energy costs. NOTE THE ASYMMETRY THIS CREATES WITH THE ALUNORTE EVENT: China's alumina cost floor is rising for domestic reasons at the same time as roughly 3 Mt/y of non-Chinese seaborne supply goes to half rate. The two are independent and they push the same way.

prices.label: Bauxite (SMM imported index / Guinea CIF China)
prices.note: Carried at the 06-Aug-2026 SMM Bauxite Weekly Review - no newer weekly review has published at this compile (the cadence is Thursday, so the next print is 13-August, tomorrow). SMM Imported Bauxite Index $71.57/mt, UP $0.70 week-on-week, Guinea CIF $70-74/mt (average +$1 w/w), Guinea FOB $38-42/mt (average +$1 w/w). CORROBORATION CARRIED FROM 11-AUGUST: SMM's alumina cost review states that imported bauxite prices 'sustained their upward trend in July, serving as the core driver behind the cost surge', citing elevated ocean freight and the Guinea rainy season reducing shipments, plus slow domestic Chinese mine resumption - to the point that 'some alumina producers have been forced to adjust production schedules'. SMM's forward view: 'no clear timeline has emerged for domestic supply recovery, while imported ore shipments are expected to shrink further amid the rainy season. Bauxite prices are likely to hold high and steady, with import quotes potentially edging slightly higher.' A STRUCTURAL DEVELOPMENT THIS RUN, NOT A PRICE MOVE: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through MONTHLY TENDERS, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and additional output sold via monthly spot tenders; CEO Patrice L'Huillier named Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. Monthly tendering adds genuine public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source and simultaneously shifts volume from contract to spot, which raises price variance in an already tight rainy-season market. THE NEXT SCHEDULED HARD DATAPOINT REMAINS THE GUINEA AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, still under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. DRIVER DOWN, UNCHANGED: Chinese refinery bauxite inventories at roughly 94 days of cover. This remains the best-evidenced upward-trending input on the whole board.

logistics.label: Strait of Hormuz transit
logistics.note: EFFECTIVELY CLOSED TO COMMERCIAL SHIPPING, DAY 164 SINCE THE 28-FEBRUARY SHUTDOWN. THE DIRECTION OF TRAVEL HARDENED FURTHER THIS RUN: SMM's 12-August wire describes the US-Iran negotiations over reopening the strait as STALLED, and attributes aluminium's move to its highest level since June directly to that stall plus record-low exchange inventories. That is one step beyond the 10-August Iranian Foreign Ministry position that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues and that no joint statement with Oman has been finalised. THE COMMERCIALLY BINDING CONSTRAINT IS INSURANCE, NOT DIPLOMACY, AND THAT IS THE POINT THAT KEEPS BEING PROVED: the 05-August routing announcement moved the aluminium curve by roughly $35/t within a session while physical transits stayed near 2 per day against a pre-crisis norm of about 73. The observable that would actually matter is war-risk cover falling from roughly 30 times pre-crisis pricing, or P&I clubs restoring cover. Neither has been publicly reported. Roughly 9% of global primary aluminium supply exits through this corridor; the trade geography here is public-domain and generic, not any single company's routing.

logistics.label: Red Sea / Bab al Mandeb corridor
logistics.note: Unchanged in substance and it should not be conflated with Hormuz. Most large container lines moved Asia-Europe services to the Cape of Good Hope as a RED SEA decision, which says nothing about Hormuz transit. Reading the two together overstates the Hormuz effect on containerised trade. Of the nine largest container carriers, 4 advisories describe stopping Hormuz or Gulf service, 3 describe reduced or escorted service still running, and 2 make no claim either way. For aluminium the relevant leg is bulk and breakbulk out of the Gulf, not the container network.

logistics.label: Gulf war-risk insurance
logistics.note: War-risk cover for a VLCC transit is estimated at roughly 30 times pre-crisis pricing, with a per-voyage premium of the order of $10m, and six P&I clubs - Gard, Skuld, North Standard, London P&I Club, American Club and Steamship Mutual - have withdrawn cover. THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT AND IT IS WHY A DIPLOMATIC HEADLINE DOES NOT REOPEN THE CORRIDOR. Underwriters price observed attack frequency and observed transit counts, not communiques. With transits at 2 per day against 73, an oil spill of roughly 390 square kilometres off Oman from a damaged tanker, 14 tankers running AIS-dark in the last 24 hours and Tehran publicly hardening on 10-August, there is nothing in the observable record that would justify an underwriter cutting rates this week. Any premium argument that assumes a rapid normalisation of freight and insurance is arguing against the pricing mechanism itself.

headlines.title: THE LARGEST ALUMINA REFINERY OUTSIDE CHINA IS RUNNING AT HALF RATE. Norsk Hydro disclosed at 07:01 CEST on 11-August that Alunorte, in Barcarena, Para, Brazil - 6.3 million tonnes a year of nameplate alumina capacity - has reduced production to 50 percent after being informed by its gas supplier CELBA, part of the New Fortress Group, of disruptions to natural gas availability. CELBA also owns the gas terminal infrastructure in Barcarena. Hydro states the refinery has implemented contingency measures including purchasing spot gas volumes, requesting direct access to the Barcarena LNG receiving and regasification terminal, and temporarily reducing production to align with available gas; it will ramp back up 'as soon as gas availability normalizes'. THE COMPANY'S OWN QUANTIFICATION: potential Q3-2026 financial impact for the Bauxite & Alumina segment from reduced production and from purchasing gas above the contract price 'may be USD 75 to 100 million', with the full impact described as uncertain. WHY THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ITEM ON THE PAGE: roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina output is off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period. Cheap alumina - around 10-11% of the metal price against a 15-17% decade norm - has been the single largest reason smelter margins expanded faster than the metal price through 2026. This is the first credible threat to that, and it arrives while the Chinese alumina cost floor is already rising on bauxite. IT IS BULLISH FOR THE METAL AND POTENTIALLY NEGATIVE FOR SMELTER MARGINS AT THE SAME TIME, which is why it is tagged on the margin lens. Public company disclosure under Section 5-12 of the Norwegian Securities Trading Act.

A FIFTH NEW CYCLE HIGH, AND THE HIGHEST OFFICIAL CASH SINCE 22-JUNE. The 11-August LME official put cash at $3,373.00, up $45.50 (+1.37%), and the three-month at $3,374.00, up $53.50 (+1.61%) - both the highest official prints since 22-June-2026, when cash settled $3,405.00. Bloomberg's 11-August coverage framed the move as aluminium extending its rally after the Brazilian refinery cut output to 50%, and as a seven-week high with the Hormuz impasse threatening supply. THE BACKWARDATION LASTED ONE SESSION. Cash $3,373.00 settled $1.00 BELOW the three-month at $3,374.00 - a CONTANGO - reversing the $7.00 backwardation of 10-August in a single day, because the three-month rose $53.50 against cash's $45.50. SPREAD AND FLAT PRICE MOVED IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS. This page named that reversal yesterday as the specific test and warned the $7.00 was 'one session old' and that single-session flips 'reverse routinely'. THE RUNNING TALLY IS THE POINT: since the 05-August routing announcement removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure, the front end has rebuilt for one session out of seven while flat price posted FIVE new cycle highs. Three of the eight August sessions have closed in contango and the front end has not held a premium two sessions running since 04-August. PROPORTION IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: $1.00 is 0.03% of cash, so the accurate description is 'no prompt premium', not 'prompt surplus'. But it sits $7.48 below the July mean of +$6.48, and a market paying more for forward metal than for prompt metal is being driven by expectation rather than by immediate physical need.

A 30TH CONSECUTIVE DRAW, AND A BETTER-SOURCED SUPERLATIVE. LME aluminium stock fell 1,500 t to 253,400 t on 11-August. SMM's 12-August wire describes LME warehouse inventories sitting near 250,000 tonnes as their LOWEST SINCE NOVEMBER 1990 - a longer-dated and better-sourced framing than the 'lowest this century' wording this page has used, and it is adopted here. The same wire reports LME aluminium at its highest since June, around $3,337/t on 11-August and up more than 8% since the end of June, attributing the bid to stalled US-Iran negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz - a route that once carried around 10% of global aluminium production - and notes that new supply from China and Indonesia has been unable to offset the inventory decline. It also carries Norsk Hydro's public warning that the global aluminium deficit could exceed 900,000 tonnes this year if Hormuz trade is not normalised. THE RATE HAS STOPPED SLOWING: six of the last seven sessions drew exactly 1,500 t, against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July.

A US GREENFIELD SMELTER IS NOW IN COURT. Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond filed a motion on 11-August in the US District Court for the Northern District of Oklahoma seeking a preliminary injunction to halt construction of the proposed US$4 billion Oklahoma Primary Aluminum smelter at Inola while his lawsuit to block the project proceeds. The plant would exceed 750,000 tonnes a year and is planned as a 60:40 venture between Emirates Global Aluminium and Century Aluminum. If granted, the injunction would prevent site preparation, land alteration, foundation work and other construction. The motion comes ahead of the town's construction moratorium expiring on 28-August. Drummond cites potential environmental, agricultural, water and electricity-grid impacts, including expected continuous power demand of more than 1,000 MW. The developers dispute the allegations and say the motion contains mischaracterisations that overlook scientific and regulatory facts. WHY IT MATTERS: the bearish case on this page rests substantially on scheduled Western capacity additions. This is the first of those to face a live legal challenge, and it is a reminder that permitted-and-announced is not the same as built - power and permitting are the binding constraints on new Western smelting, not capital.

INDONESIAN CAPACITY KEEPS ADVANCING ON SCHEDULE, WHICH IS THE STANDING CAP ON THIS RALLY. SMM reported on 12-August that Oriental Yuhong's Hongjia Industrial Coatings won the anti-corrosion contract for Taijing Aluminum Indonesia's 600,000 tonne aluminium project in the Morowali Industrial Park, jointly invested by China's Xinfa Group and Tsingshan Group and using 600 kA large-scale electrolytic cells. The first phase, 300,000 tonnes, is expected to commence production in 2026. Contract awards for site protection systems are a construction-progress signal rather than a production signal, and should be read as such - but they are consistent with SMM's July statistics showing outside-China DAILY AVERAGE output rising 1.6% month-on-month even as the year-on-year total fell 6.7%.

GUINEA MOVES ITS STATE BAUXITE TO MONTHLY TENDERS. Reported on 11-August and published by SMM on 12-August: Guinea's Mines Minister Bouna Sylla said state-owned Nimba Mining Company will sell bauxite to global traders and miners through monthly tenders. Nimba CEO Patrice L'Huillier said the company plans to secure trading partners through agreements setting a minimum guaranteed annual sales volume, while selling additional output via monthly spot tenders; Sylla said the aim is to let Nimba operate on a par with international mining companies, naming Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta as potential partners. WHY IT IS MIXED: monthly tendering adds public price discovery to the world's most important seaborne bauxite source, which is useful. It also shifts volume from contract to spot in a market already tight on rainy-season shipments, which raises the variance of the single input SMM identifies as the core driver of rising Chinese alumina cost.

THE HORMUZ TALKS ARE DESCRIBED AS STALLED, NOT ADVANCING. SMM's 12-August wire attributes the move to highs explicitly to 'stalled US-Iran negotiations over reopening the Strait of Hormuz', raising fears of prolonged Middle East supply disruption on a route that once carried around 10% of global aluminium production. That is consistent with, and one step further than, Iran's Foreign Ministry position published on 10-August that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues and that no joint statement with Oman has been finalised. THE COMMERCIALLY RELEVANT DISTINCTION IS UNCHANGED AND WORTH REPEATING: an announcement is not a restoration of insurance. The 05-August routing announcement moved the aluminium curve by roughly $35/t while physical transits stayed near 2 per day against a pre-crisis norm of about 73. The observable that would actually matter is war-risk cover falling from roughly 30 times pre-crisis pricing, or P&I clubs restoring cover - neither has been publicly reported.

THE COMPLEX ROSE TOGETHER BUT ALUMINIUM'S FRONT END WENT THE OTHER WAY. On the 11-August three-month official aluminium rose +1.61%, zinc +0.54%, copper +0.46% and lead +0.26%, with only nickel lower at -0.82% - a second consecutive four-to-one board. backtest.verdict: These condition indicators showed NO predictive edge when tested: a 38.4% directional hit rate against a 71.2% naive 'always higher' baseline over the same sample, and forward returns after 'tightening' readings averaged 1.8% versus 7.04% after 'loosening' readings. They are therefore published as a read on CURRENT market condition only — not as a price forecast. The forward baseline and probability range above are the forward-looking view.
backtest.caveat: Measured on overlapping 13-week windows of weekly LME data (99 observations, 2024-05-24 to 2026-05-15). Overlapping windows overstate significance and the sample spans a single, largely rising market — evidence in either direction is weak.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

earnings.note: Q2-2026 BEAT AND A HIGHER Q3 GUIDE: adjusted EBITDA attributable $326.9m against $315-335m guidance and $231.4m in Q1; net sales $752.1m (Q1 $649.2m); shipments 130,632 t (Q1 122,865 t); net income attributable $249.3m; diluted EPS $2.39; adjusted EPS $2.46. Q3-2026 guidance $325-345m. Liquidity $784.9m with cash $343.4m; cash exceeded total debt as of end-July after a $94.3m 2025 45X refund was received. Q2 adjustments included $61.3m for an Iceland equipment failure (net of tax) and $10.7m of Mt. Holly expansion cost. THE PUREST US AND SECTION-232 READ IN THE PEER SET, AND IT CONFIRMS THAT THE 2026 PRICE AND TARIFF STRUCTURE IS CONVERTING TO CASH. Adjusted EBITDA rose 41% sequentially on a 6.3% increase in shipments, which is operating leverage on price and premium rather than on volume. The last 90 Mt. Holly pots have been restarted, taking the plant to full capacity for the first time since 2015, and Grundartangi Line 2 is near full - so the volume base steps up again into Q3, which is why the guide moved higher despite Q2 already beating. THE COST-SIDE SIGNAL MATTERS FOR THE WHOLE BOARD: management again cited UNFAVOURABLE RAW-MATERIAL PRICE REALISATION as the principal EBITDA headwind, the second consecutive quarter it has done so. That is the same message the input basket carries - a firming alumina and bauxite leg partly offsetting a falling energy leg - and it is the reason a rising LME does not translate one-for-one into producer margin.

earnings.note: Net profit SAR 2.18bn (+13% y/y, +33% q/q); revenue SAR 10.9bn (+16% y/y, +24% q/q); gross profit SAR 3.39bn (-4%) and operating profit SAR 2.36bn (-8%). A clean example of the split running through this whole peer season: the top line and the bottom line rose on higher commodity prices across all business units and higher aluminium and gold sales volumes, while GROSS and OPERATING profit FELL on input and logistics cost inflation - here concentrated in phosphate (sulphur, freight) rather than in the aluminium chain. Net profit was additionally helped by higher finance income, lower finance costs and a larger share of equity-accounted profits, so the headline overstates the operating improvement. The generic read for the aluminium market is the same one Century and Hindalco delivered from opposite ends of the integration spectrum: a rising metal price is not converting one-for-one into margin wherever the input leg is bought rather than owned.

earnings.note: Q1 FY27 net income $164m, +71% year-on-year; adjusted EBITDA $516m, +24% year-on-year; net sales $5.8bn, +23% year-on-year. Results discussed on a call held 05-Aug, ahead of parent Hindalco's Q1 FY27 board meeting on 07-Aug. The first DOWNSTREAM read of the disruption quarter and it points the same way as the upstream set: rolled-products economics expanded rather than being squeezed by a high metal price, with the gain attributed publicly to metal price lag and cost performance. That matters for the balance argument because the standard bear case against a high LME is that converters destroy demand; a 23% sales increase with a 24% EBITDA increase is not consistent with that. It also sets the tone into Hindalco's own print on 07-Aug, where management has guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation and the upstream EBITDA strip has risen four consecutive quarters.

earnings.note: Q2-2026 profit attributable to equity holders BHD 64.9m (US$172.5m), +164% y/y; Q2 EBITDA US$295m; EPS 46 fils. H1 profit BHD 140.2m (US$372.8m), +228% y/y; EPS 99 fils. OPERATIONALLY THE WEAKEST PRINT IN THE PEER SET: Q2 net finished production 155,469 t, DOWN 61% y/y, and sales volume 280,799 t, -32% y/y, with Lines 1, 2 and 3 still under controlled shutdown on regional tensions and raw-material availability. Value-added product was 195,891 t, 70% of shipments. THE SHARPEST ILLUSTRATION ON THIS BOARD OF WHAT THE 2026 MARKET IS ACTUALLY REWARDING: a producer can lose 61% of its output year-on-year and still nearly triple half-year profit, because average LME rose 46% y/y to $3,576/t in Q2. It also quantifies the supply loss the deficit rests on - Alba's own read put the Q2 global deficit at 934,000 t including China and 626,000 t excluding it, with global supply contracting about 1% mainly on Middle East disruption. Management explicitly framed the curtailments as preserving flexibility for a swift recovery when conditions improve, which is the restart option the bearish case depends on. Separately Alba is progressing its US$2.2bn acquisition of Aluminium Dunkerque, about 300,000 t/y and the largest EU smelter.

status.impact: The largest single supply event on this page. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised alumina off the seaborne balance for an unspecified period, against +75,000 t/y of EU primary metal returning in Q4
status.update: DISCLOSED 11-AUG-2026 AT 07:01 CEST UNDER SECTION 5-12 OF THE NORWEGIAN SECURITIES TRADING ACT. Alunorte in Barcarena, Para, Brazil - 6.3 Mt/y nameplate and the largest alumina refinery outside China - has REDUCED PRODUCTION TO 50 PERCENT after being informed by gas supplier CELBA, part of the New Fortress Group, of disruptions to natural gas availability; CELBA also owns the Barcarena gas terminal infrastructure. Contingency measures: purchasing spot gas volumes, requesting direct access to the Barcarena LNG receiving and regasification terminal, and temporarily reducing production to align with available gas. Hydro will begin ramping up 'as soon as gas availability normalizes'. The supplier has indicated it is seeking to source gas on market terms compatible with its current financial situation; Alunorte says it will continue pursuing long-term alternative gas supplies while preserving its rights under the Gas Supply Agreement. FINANCIAL GUIDANCE, THE COMPANY'S OWN: potential Q3-2026 impact for Bauxite & Alumina from reduced production and from purchasing gas above the contract price 'may be USD 75 to 100 million'; the full impact is described as uncertain. SEPARATELY AND UNCHANGED: the Slovalco restart of 75,000 t/y agreed with the Slovak government on 01-July, including a long-term power contract with a state-owned utility and EU ETS indirect-cost compensation, is still targeted for Q4-2026 and remains the clearest dated European primary supply addition. Hydro has also previously declared force majeure on aluminium sales following the Qatalum shutdown on natural gas shortages.

THE HORMUZ REGIME IS UNCHANGED IN SUBSTANCE AND HARDER IN TONE: SMM's 12-August wire describes the US-Iran reopening negotiations as STALLED, one step beyond the 10-August Iranian Foreign Ministry position that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues and that no joint statement with Oman has been finalised. A THIRD DEVELOPMENT WORTH RECORDING ON THE BAUXITE LEG: Guinea's Mines Minister said state-owned Nimba Mining will move to selling bauxite through monthly tenders to global traders and miners, which shifts volume from contract to spot on the world's most important seaborne bauxite lane. THE GENERIC COMMERCIAL POINT IS UNCHANGED: the binding constraint on the Gulf lanes is the insurance market, not the diplomatic channel - underwriters reprice on observed attack frequency and observed transit counts, which is why the 05-August announcement moved the aluminium curve by roughly $35/t while the physical corridor did not follow. flows.note: About 9% of global primary supply exits via the Strait of Hormuz and more than 80% of Gulf metal is exported; Gulf output was -34.5% y/y in June, and on the published aggregate the IAI's June-2026 release (20-July-2026) showed global primary output down 1.5% y/y; a widely repeated 'outside-China -6.7% y/y in July' figure could not be traced to a dated IAI release at this refresh and is not carried here. THE 05-AUG IRAN-OMAN AGREEMENT ON ROUTE COORDINATES IS THE FIRST CONCRETE STEP TOWARD A REOPENING, and it is deliberately NOT treated as one here: the route is temporary (two to four months by Iran's own account), both existing lanes would close in its favour, Tehran says safe navigation is not restored, and the published count on the day was eight vessels against roughly 130-140 pre-war. catalysts.text: THE 12-AUGUST LME OFFICIAL - AND SPECIFICALLY WHETHER THE CONTANGO WIDENS INTO A SIXTH NEW HIGH. This is the highest-information event on the calendar. Three reads in order of value: (1) does the cash-3M spread recover toward flat, or does it widen further into contango while flat price keeps climbing - a widening contango into new highs would be the clearest evidence yet that the physical market is not following the financial one; (2) does the stock draw hold at the 1,500 t/day rate that has run for six of the last seven sessions, or does it break either way; (3) does the complex stay together, and specifically whether copper's and zinc's backwardations keep widening while aluminium's front end stays flat - that divergence is currently the single most informative cross-metal signal on the board.

THE FIRST PUBLIC SEABORNE ALUMINA PRINT AFTER THE ALUNORTE DISCLOSURE. Norsk Hydro's 11-August notice that the 6.3 Mt/y refinery is running at 50 percent is a supply fact without a price attached; no public transaction dated after the disclosure was found at this compile. The next SMM-reported seaborne trade - the last two were $356/mt FOB East Australia dealt 05-August and $365/mt CIF Malaysia dealt 07-August - is the datapoint that converts a headline into a cost. Watch also for any Hydro update on gas availability at Barcarena, since the company has said it will ramp back up as soon as supply normalises, which makes the duration the whole question.

SMM BAUXITE WEEKLY REVIEW - DUE TOMORROW. The cadence is Thursday and the last print was 06-August at an SMM Imported Bauxite Index of $71.57/mt (+$0.70 w/w), Guinea CIF $70-74/mt. SMM's forward view is that imported ore shipments will shrink further amid the rainy season and that import quotes could edge slightly higher. This is the highest-frequency public series in the input basket and the best-evidenced upward-trending cost line, and it now carries extra weight because bauxite is the mechanism by which China's alumina cost floor rises independently of the Alunorte outage.

MONTHLY CARBON SETTLEMENT WINDOW - PREBAKED ANODES, CALCINED PETROLEUM COKE AND COAL TAR PITCH. Prebaked anodes are the largest non-energy line in the smelter input basket and the July mark of RMB 5,683/t stands until this settles. Both feedstock legs point up into it: Brent at $89.44 and coal at $129.30, +15.76% year-on-year. Landing in the same fortnight as an alumina supply shock, this is the fortnight's most consequential scheduled input datapoint and the main near-term threat to the margin expansion running through peer earnings.

OKLAHOMA INOLA SMELTER - INJUNCTION RULING AND MORATORIUM EXPIRY. The Oklahoma Attorney General filed on 11-August for a preliminary injunction halting construction of the US$4bn, >750 kt/y EGA-Century 60:40 venture; the town's construction moratorium expires 28-August. A granted injunction would prevent site preparation, land alteration and foundation work. This is the first dated legal test of whether announced Western capacity actually arrives, and the bearish supply case on this page depends materially on the answer.

Q4-2026 MJP PREMIUM NEGOTIATIONS OPEN. Q3-2026 settled at $395/t CIF Japan on 06-July, an 11-year high, against Q2's $350-353. Talks conventionally open around late August and conclude late September. THE TWO SIDES MOVED APART SLIGHTLY TODAY. Sellers gained: SMM now describes the Hormuz talks as stalled, exchange inventory is at its lowest since November 1990, Alba's Lines 1-3 remain curtailed, EGA is still restoring, and roughly 3 Mt/y of seaborne alumina just went to half rate. Buyers gained too: the yen sits at 159.31, and the LME front end has now failed to hold a prompt premium for two consecutive sessions since 04-August, which is direct evidence against paying more for prompt physical metal. The Q4-26 figure on this page is a SCENARIO RANGE of $320-420, not an assessment.

It fills at this event. As the largest Chinese producer, Chalco is also the cleanest public read on whether the rising domestic alumina cost floor is reaching the P&L.

PRESS METAL (8869.KL) Q2-2026 RESULTS. Press Metal reported a record MYR 624.5m net profit for Q1-2026 on 28-May, its third consecutive record quarter, after MYR 592.14m in Q4-2025 - the Q4-25 figure was back-filled into the earnings_history series this run. No Q2-2026 figure has published yet. As the largest South-East Asian smelter it is the cleanest read on whether the margin expansion visible in Western peers extends to Asian producers.

IRAN-OMAN SAFE-NAVIGATION MECHANISM - WATCH FOR A SIGNED JOINT STATEMENT AND FOR INSURANCE, NOT FOR HEADLINES. SMM's 12-August wire describes the negotiations as stalled; Iran's Foreign Ministry confirmed on 10-August that no joint statement has been finalised and declined to discuss transit fees. The distinction that matters commercially is between an announcement and a restoration of insurance: the 05-August announcement moved the aluminium curve by roughly $35/t while transits stayed at about 2 per day against a norm of 73. The observable that would actually matter is war-risk cover falling from roughly 30 times pre-crisis, or P&I clubs restoring cover.

GUINEA BAUXITE - AUGUST LONG-TERM CONTRACT, AND NOW A STRUCTURAL CHANGE IN HOW STATE VOLUME IS SOLD. The August long-term contract remains under negotiation against July's settlement of $70-71.5/mt. Separately, Guinea's Mines Minister said on 11-August that state-owned Nimba Mining will sell bauxite through MONTHLY TENDERS to global traders and miners, with minimum guaranteed annual volumes under partner agreements and the balance sold spot; Mercuria, Glencore, Rio Tinto and Vedanta were named as potential partners. More public price discovery, and more spot variance, on the world's most important seaborne bauxite lane.

SMM WEEKLY FLUORIDE SALTS, SILICON AND MAGNESIUM REVIEWS. Three input rows on this page are waiting on weekly marks: aluminium fluoride and cryolite (the last verified public review found is dated 21-MAY-2026 and was explicitly REJECTED as stale rather than appended), and silicon and magnesium (last sourced marks 06-August). Each new print appends one sourced pair to the relevant hist series. No new mark was returned this run, so nothing was appended.

SLOVALCO RESTART - 75,000 t/y. Hydro reached agreement with the Slovak government on 01-July-2026 to resume production, with start-up expected in Q4-2026. This is the first genuine European primary capacity return of the cycle and the clearest dated EU supply addition, which matters directly to the European Duty Unpaid premium. It sits on the same balance sheet as Alunorte, which is now running at half rate - Hydro is simultaneously the clearest European supply addition and the source of the largest alumina supply loss of the cycle.

risks.text: THE RALLY IS NOW FIVE NEW HIGHS OLD WITH ESSENTIALLY NO CURVE CONFIRMATION, AND THAT IS THE CENTRAL RISK ON THIS PAGE TODAY. Monday's $7.00 backwardation lasted exactly one session before the 11-August official put cash $1.00 BELOW the three-month. Since 05-August the front end has rebuilt for one session out of seven while flat price made five new cycle highs, and three of eight August sessions have closed in contango. A market that will pay progressively more for forward metal but not for prompt metal is being driven by expectation rather than by immediate physical need - and expectations reprice far faster than physical balances do. The specific vulnerability is that the two expectations carrying this move, a permanently shut Hormuz and a structurally short alumina market, are both headline-driven and both reversible within a single session, as 05-August demonstrated. TREND UP: the risk this desk described as partially resolved yesterday re-opened in full today, and it re-opened while price was making a new high, which is the worse of the two ways it could have happened.

THE ALUMINA COST FLOOR IS NOW RISING FROM TWO INDEPENDENT DIRECTIONS AT ONCE, AND THIS IS THE BIGGEST CHANGE TO THE RISK PICTURE IN WEEKS. Norsk Hydro disclosed on 11-August that Alunorte - 6.3 Mt/y, the largest alumina refinery outside China - cut production to 50 percent after its gas supplier notified disruptions to natural gas availability, guiding a potential Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact of US$75-100 million. Roughly 3 Mt/y of annualised seaborne-capable supply is at half rate for an unspecified period. Separately, SMM measured China's weighted-average FULL alumina production cost rising RMB 37/mt month-on-month in July to RMB 2,718/mt, attributed almost entirely to bauxite, with August guided to RMB 2,700-2,820/mt and import quotes expected to edge higher. WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE METAL PRICE: alumina at roughly 10.6% of the 11-August three-month official, against a 15-17% decade norm, is the single largest reason producer margins have expanded faster than the metal price through 2026. Every set of peer results on this page rests on it. A move back toward the norm compresses margins even in a rising metal tape. TREND UP, AND THE IMPACT RATING IS RAISED TO HIGH: this stopped being a slow cost drift and became a dated, quantified, operator-disclosed supply event.

SUPPLY OUTSIDE CHINA IS STILL RETURNING ON A PUBLISHED SCHEDULE, AND THE COMPOSITION IS SHIFTING EAST. SMM statistics show outside-China DAILY AVERAGE production rose 1.6% month-on-month in July even as the year-on-year total fell 6.7%, with SMM stating explicitly that the renewed Middle East conflict 'has not affected smelter production again'. Dated additions: Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026, Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y at New Madrid by year-end, Mt. Holly already back at full capacity, EGA restoring Al Taweelah cell by cell, and now Taijing Aluminum Indonesia's 600,000 t Morowali project with a 300,000 t first phase expected to commence production in 2026. A market priced on a supply shock is exposed to that shock unwinding on a schedule. THE COUNTER-EVIDENCE IS REAL AND IS CARRIED RATHER THAN SUPPRESSED: SMM's own 12-August wire says new supply from China and Indonesia has been UNABLE TO OFFSET the LME inventory decline, and the Oklahoma injunction motion shows Western additions are not a safe assumption. TREND FLAT: one dated Asian addition advanced and one Western addition was legally challenged in the same 24 hours - the net schedule risk is genuinely unchanged today.

END DEMAND REMAINS THE WEAKEST LINK AND THE PRICE IS RATIONING IT HARDER AT EVERY NEW HIGH. SMM reports Chinese downstream processing in its traditional consumption off-season with operating rates under pressure, purchase willingness subdued, and prices above 24,000 yuan/mt suppressing downstream procurement; central China cargo has been clearing at a discount to the futures contract, with the bid attributed to traders and spot-futures arbitrage rather than to consumers. SMM's 12-August count also shows China's secondary aluminium alloy ingot inventory rising 330 mt - small, but a build in the one series the bullish case needs to keep falling. A rally whose marginal buyer is an arbitrageur is structurally more fragile than one whose marginal buyer is a fabricator, and the contango on the LME front end is the same fact expressed on a different exchange. TREND UP: the metal price rose another 1.6% into an off-season, and a secondary inventory build appeared.

A CREDIBLE HORMUZ REOPENING REMAINS THE LARGEST SINGLE DOWNSIDE PRICE RISK, AND IT MOVED FURTHER AWAY AGAIN. SMM's 12-August wire describes the US-Iran negotiations over reopening the strait as STALLED and attributes aluminium's move to its highest since June directly to that stall, alongside record-low inventories. That is one step beyond the 10-August Iranian Foreign Ministry position that the strait will not reopen while the US naval posture continues and that no joint statement with Oman has been finalised. THE RISK HAS NOT GONE AWAY AND SHOULD NOT BE WRITTEN DOWN TOO FAR: the 05-August routing announcement alone removed roughly $35/t of prompt structure within a session, which is a live demonstration of how much of this price is geopolitical premium and how quickly it can be withdrawn. The observable that would matter is war-risk cover falling from roughly 30 times pre-crisis, or P&I clubs restoring cover - neither has been publicly reported. TREND DOWN: the near-term probability of the bearish trigger fell again on the newswire framing.

LIQUIDITY AND RATES ARE THE CLEANEST MECHANISM BY WHICH THIS RALLY STALLS WITHOUT A SINGLE PHYSICAL FACT CHANGING, AND A US INFLATION PRINT IS IMMINENT. Trading Economics marks the US 10-year at 4.694% on 12-August, marginally below the 4.713% carried yesterday, with the dollar ticking higher into the inflation release and DXY at 99.844. Industrial metals are positioning-sensitive: long-dated financing costs raise the cost of carrying inventory and of holding commodity length, and they bite hardest exactly when a rally is carried by financial rather than consumer demand - which the contango on the front end suggests is the case here. TREND FLAT: yields eased marginally rather than extending, so the channel is holding rather than tightening. The scheduled inflation print is what could change that in a single session.

THE PHYSICAL DRAW HAS STOPPED ACCELERATING AND IS NOW RUNNING AT A FIXED RATE, WHICH IS EASY TO MISS BEHIND A HEADLINE 30TH CONSECUTIVE DRAW. LME stock fell 1,500 t to 253,400 t, and six of the last seven sessions have taken out exactly 1,500 t against 2,000-2,400 t/day in late July. In China, SMM has reported the ingot destocking pace narrowing. The direction of travel is still tightening and the absolute level is extraordinary - SMM frames it as the lowest since November 1990 - but a constant-rate draw into a contango is precisely the configuration in which a backwardation appears and then fails to hold, which is exactly what happened on 10 and 11 August. TREND FLAT: the deceleration itself has stabilised; the rate is steady rather than worsening.

THE AUGUST CARBON SETTLEMENT AROUND THE 17TH-18TH IS THE NEXT SCHEDULED MARGIN EVENT AND BOTH FEEDSTOCK LEGS POINT UP. Prebaked anodes are the largest non-energy line in the smelter input basket and settle monthly alongside calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch; the July mark of RMB 5,683/t stands until then. Brent at $89.44 after two consecutive daily gains feeds green coke through refinery economics, and coal at $129.30 is up 15.76% year-on-year on Trading Economics' board, feeding coal tar pitch. A high August anode settlement landing in the same fortnight as an alumina supply shock would compress the margin expansion that is currently driving every set of peer earnings on this page. TREND UP: both feedstock proxies rose again into the settlement window.

DATA-INTEGRITY RISK IS ACTIVE, NOT THEORETICAL, AND IT MATERIALISED AGAIN THIS RUN - THIS TIME ON A PRIMARY PAGE. At this compile the Westmetall ENGLISH OVERVIEW was still serving a stale 10-August board while the cache-busted GERMAN overview and the cache-busted per-metal tables both carried the 11-August session and agreed exactly. A single-source compile off the English overview would have published a completely flat day - no price change, no stock change, no FX change - on a session in which cash moved $45.50 and the curve flipped. THAT IS THE FOURTH DISTINCT CACHE INCIDENT LOGGED (31-Jul per-metal tables, 04-Aug English overview, 11-Aug per-metal tables, 12-Aug English overview) AND THE SECOND ON AN OVERVIEW PAGE. The mitigation - fetching both language overviews plus cache-busted per-metal tables and requiring exact agreement - caught it for the fourth time. TREND UP: incidents are now occurring on consecutive runs and have moved onto the primary overview pages rather than the secondary tables, so the frequency and the severity of the failure mode have both increased even though the control is working.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY. A dedicated search this run returned no new public assessment, settlement or negotiation print for any premium row. Every premium value and its assessment date are CARRIED UNCHANGED and are explicitly stale rather than silently re-dated. The Q4-2026 MJP figure is a SCENARIO RANGE of $320-420 derived from public facts, NOT an assessment, and must not be read as one.

NO ALUMINA PRICE ON THIS PAGE HAS BEEN CHANGED IN RESPONSE TO THE ALUNORTE OUTAGE, because no public seaborne print dated after the 11-August disclosure was found. A supply headline of that size invites an estimated mark, and an estimated mark would be a fabrication. THE ALUNORTE REDUCTION IS EXPLICITLY TEMPORARY AND OF UNKNOWN DURATION. Norsk Hydro states it will begin ramping up to full production as soon as gas availability normalises, and that its supplier is seeking to source gas. The US$75-100m figure is the company's own guidance for a POTENTIAL Q3-2026 Bauxite & Alumina impact and is described by the company as uncertain. It should not be treated as a realised loss or as a permanent capacity removal.

TWO SUPERLATIVES ARE USED CAREFULLY AND ON DIFFERENT SOURCING. The 30th consecutive draw is arithmetic from the Westmetall stock series. 'Lowest since November 1990' is SMM's 12-August newswire framing of LME inventories near 250,000 t and is attributed to them; it replaces the 'lowest this century' wording this page used previously because it is better sourced and longer dated.

ALL PREMIUMS ARE QUOTED IN $/t. US premium rows are TARIFF-INFLATED BY CONSTRUCTION: at the 11-August cash settlement the Section 232 leg alone is 0.50 x $3,373.00 = $1,686.50/t. That decomposition is arithmetic on a verified statutory rate, not a market assessment, and it is not a premium.

CORROBORATING MARKS FROM DIFFERENT BASES ARE QUOTED SEPARATELY AND NEVER BLENDED INTO THE OFFICIAL ROWS. Trading Economics' CFD marks $3,360.55 for 11-August and SMM's wire reports around $3,337/t; both sit BELOW the 13:20 official, which is the reverse of the usual pattern. Similarly the $356/mt FOB East Australia and $365/mt CIF Malaysia alumina trades are load-port and delivered prices respectively and are not spliced into one series.

THE ELLIOTT WAVE PANELS ARE TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, AND NO PIVOT HAS BEEN LABELLED AT TODAY'S EXTREME. The $3,374.00 three-month official is the live high, not a confirmed reversal point. The published wave-(v) equality target of $3,373 being met to within $1.00 is recorded because it was published in advance, but a met measurement is the point of maximum count risk, not minimum.

PEER EARNINGS HISTORY CARRIES EXACT PUBLICLY VERIFIED FIGURES ONLY AND GAPS STAY GAPS. Press Metal's Q4-2025 net profit of MYR 592.14m was back-filled this run; Q2-2025 and Q3-2025 remain empty because the only available Q2-2025 number was an analyst projection, which is a forecast and not a reported result. Chalco's Q2-2026 slot is deliberately empty pending the late-August interim.

INPUT-BASKET SERIES ARE SPARSE BY DESIGN. Only copper has a genuine daily public series and it is rolled every run on the same 15 sessions as the LME Board. Rows with no public series - smelter power, cathode and graphite blocks, Ti-B grain refiner - carry no history at all rather than estimated points. Fluoride salts remain on a rejected 21-May mark rather than a spliced stale one. Nothing here is interpolated.

EVERYTHING PUBLISHED ON THIS PAGE IS PUBLIC INFORMATION AND GENERIC MARKET INTELLIGENCE. There are no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary of any organisation. The only company-specific content is publicly listed-company disclosure and press, used in the peer earnings, producer status and news panels.

FORWARD-LOOKING CONTENT IS SCENARIO CONSTRUCTION, NOT FORECASTING WITH AUTHORITY. Scenario probabilities, the Q4 premium range, the Q3 alumina estimates and the wave projections are all derived from public facts and are labelled as such. Where a third-party model is quoted - Trading Economics at $3,400 for the quarter and $3,604.43 in twelve months - it is attributed and carried as a reference, not adopted as this page's view.
